If present, read `.agent-local/copilot-memory.md` before making changes in this repository.

Memory rules:
- **"Memory" in this repo means this file** — when the user says "update memory" or "save to memory", update `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
- Do not write repo knowledge or decisions to the user's `~/.claude/` directory or to `.agent-local/`. Those locations are machine-local and invisible to other contributors.
- All repo-level memory (design decisions, conventions, seed rules, naming choices) belongs in this file so it travels with the repo.
- The only exception is genuinely machine-specific state: absolute paths, local tool locations (e.g. `JQ_BIN`), or per-machine overrides. Those belong in `.agent-local/copilot-memory.md` or `env/common.env`, not in `~/.claude/`.

Respect these repo-specific rules:
- Do not start stacks, run `make start`, or launch other long-running services unless the user explicitly asks.
- It is fine to make file edits proactively when the requested change is clear.
- Preserve the dataset dimension in the scaffold even when only the `sample` dataset exists.
- Treat env files in `env/` as shell-sourced files. Quote values that contain spaces.
- On Windows Git Bash, keep Docker compose path handling compatible with native Docker on Windows.

Tracked repo notes:
- Version env files (`env/mb_versions/*.env`) are gitignored and personal — each developer creates their own from `env/mb_versions/template.env.example`. There is no shared canonical version list. Floating `.x` filenames (e.g. `1.61.1.x.env`) track the latest patch; a full 4-part filename (e.g. `1.61.1.3.env`) pins to a specific build.
- The current dataset profile is `sample-pg15`, using `metabase/qa-databases:postgres-sample-15` from `env/dwh_source/sample-pg15.env`. The sample data warehouse service is named `sample-dwh` in Docker Compose (not `sample-db`). The Metabase connection display name is `sample_dwh_pg15`.
- **No-stacks guard for `make start`**: if the user runs `make start` (or `make stop`/`make nuke`) and gets the error `No version env files found in env/mb_versions/`, do **not** just repeat the error message. Instead, ask the user if they'd like to create their first stack, then guide them through `make new` (which walks them through choosing a Metabase version and sets up the env file). Phrase it as: "It looks like you don't have any stacks configured yet. Would you like me to walk you through `make new` to create one?"
- The public workflow is `make list`, `make start`, `make stop`, `make nuke`, `make new`, `make remove`, and `make done`. When `MB_VERSION` is omitted from start/stop/nuke, each invokes `scripts/pick.sh <action>` — reads `env/mb_versions/` and `env/dwh_source/`, detects running stacks via `docker compose ls`, presents an interactive numbered menu. When `MB_VERSION` is supplied, bypasses the picker and calls the script directly.
- `make done` (`scripts/done.sh`): stops all running `mb_*` stacks (via `docker compose ls`, filters out `mb_shared`) plus shared services in one command. Uses `docker compose -p <project> stop` so volumes are preserved. Intended as an end-of-day shutdown shortcut.
- `make list` (`scripts/list-stacks.sh`): shows all configured stacks (from `env/mb_versions/*.env`) with their Metabase port and running status. Running stacks show the dataset and `→ http://localhost:<port>`.
- `make nuke` (`scripts/nuke.sh`): removes containers, the compose network, external volumes, and the seed markers under `.state/`. When called directly (not via `make remove`), it prompts to also delete the version env file; if the user confirms, it also removes the Firefox container entry (via `firefox-container.sh --remove`) and the metabot-debug-logs subfolder for that stack. Pass `--keep-env` to skip the prompt (used internally by `make remove`). `make remove` handles env deletion itself after nuking all dataset combos.
- `make new` (`scripts/new-stack.sh`): two-step drill-down — prompts for major version (e.g. `1.61`), fetches all stable builds for that major from Docker Hub (one request, `page_size=50`, filters to 4-part semver, excludes beta/rc/alpha), presents unique minor versions first, then hotfix builds for the chosen minor plus a float-on-`.x` option. Existing stacks are annotated in both menus; selecting an existing one exits cleanly. Version `0.x` uses repo `metabase/metabase` (OSS); `1.x` uses `metabase/metabase-enterprise`. Scans existing env files to suggest non-conflicting ports (max+10 for Metabase, max+10 for DB ports). Port conflicts are not auto-resolved — user edits the env file and retries.
- `make remove` (`scripts/remove-stack.sh`): shows all version env files, nukes all dataset combos for the chosen version (with `--keep-env`), removes Firefox container entries and metabot-debug-logs for each dataset combo, then deletes the env file. One entry per version (not per version+dataset combo).
- `make prune`: first removes repo-managed Metabase images whose retention window has expired, then runs `docker image prune -f` for dangling layers and `docker volume prune -f` for orphaned volumes. `scripts/nuke.sh` marks a Metabase image for cleanup once no containers still reference it; `scripts/start.sh` clears that marker when the stack is started again. Markers live under `.state/image-gc/` and default to a 30-day retention window (`IMAGE_GC_RETENTION_DAYS`, if exported in the shell).
- `scripts/common.sh` is the shared runtime layer for env loading, path normalization, stack naming, compose invocation, Metabase image refresh (pull if newer, prune old), and Metabase health waiting. Key helpers: `load_common_env` (loads `env/common.env`, pre-declares `DATASET`/`MB_VERSION` to satisfy `set -u`, configures optional tools — call this instead of repeating the inline pattern); `project_name_for <version> <dataset>` (derives the Compose project name — lives in common.sh, do not redefine it locally); `sanitize_key` (converts `.` and `-` to `_` for use in Compose project names and volume names).
- `scripts/pick.sh` calls `load_common_env` to load common settings before a stack is chosen. Running stacks detected via `docker compose ls | awk` — no jq needed for this step.
- `scripts/firefox-container.sh` creates a Firefox Multi-Account Container entry for a stack by writing directly to the default profile's `containers.json`. Called from `scripts/start.sh` after the stack is ready. Exit codes: 0 = container already existed, 1 = Firefox not installed or profile not found (silent skip), 2 = container just created (user must restart Firefox). Container name format: `mb-<MB_VERSION>-<DATASET>-<METABASE_PORT>-admin` (e.g. `mb-1.61.2.x-sample-pg15-3310-admin`). Does not stop or prompt Firefox — writes directly; Firefox overwrites the file on exit if containers were edited in a live session, so running `make start` again recreates any lost entry.
- Bootstrap uses `seed/metabase/config-pg15.yml` (Postgres) or `seed/metabase/config-mysql8.yml` (MySQL) — selected via `METABASE_CONFIG_FILE` in the dataset env file — plus `scripts/seed-metabase.sh` to create admin, analyst, and sales users, two groups, a starter collection, and a connectivity-check card.
- Seed new Metabase cards with the simplest viable approach: build direct API payloads in `scripts/seed-metabase.sh` instead of adding a separate metadata or template layer unless there is a strong reason.
- For GUI-query seeds that depend on Metabase field IDs, derive table and field IDs from live database metadata inside `scripts/seed-metabase.sh` instead of hardcoding raw IDs from one local stack.
- When deciding whether seeded cards or dashboards already exist, use `/api/collection/<id>/items` for the seeded collection rather than Metabase search results; search can return stale entries for content that no longer exists in the real collection state.
- The Metabase content seed uses the version marker in `.state/*.metabase-seeded` to decide when to reconcile new baseline content into an existing stack. The sample DWH seed uses `.state/*.sample-dwh-seeded`.
- When adding seeded Metabase cards, ask whether the card should also be attached to a dashboard; default to collection-only unless the user explicitly wants dashboard changes.
- If the user wants dashboard changes based on a locally edited dashboard, prefer extracting or importing the dashboard as a seeded artifact rather than hand-rebuilding dashboard layout in shell.
- Future datasets should be added as dataset env files plus dataset compose overlays, not as one-off compose copies.
- Shared services (Mailpit, webhook-tester, Keycloak) run as a separate Compose project (`mb_shared`) on a Docker network also named `mb_shared`. Each Metabase stack joins this network via `compose/base.yml` so it can reach shared services by hostname. `make services-up` / `make services-down` manage shared services manually. `scripts/shared-services.sh` does not source `common.sh`; it inlines its own `normalize_docker_path()` (using `cygpath -w` on Windows Git Bash). Commands: `up` (start all), `stop` (stop without removing), `down` (remove), `ensure` (start only active profiles), `ensure-network` (create `mb_shared` network without starting services — called unconditionally from `start.sh` before any stack launches).
- Shared services use Docker Compose profiles so only enabled services start. Each service has a profile: `mailpit` → `email`, `webhook-tester` → `webhooks`, `keycloak` → `saml`. `make services-up` activates all three profiles. `shared-services.sh ensure` reads `ENABLE_EMAIL`/`ENABLE_WEBHOOKS`/`ENABLE_SAML` from the environment and activates only the matching profiles — so starting a stack with only `ENABLE_SAML=true` starts Keycloak but not Mailpit or webhook-tester. `docker compose up -d --profile <x>` is idempotent, so `ensure` always calls it without a pre-check.
- Per-stack optional service flags live in the version env file: `ENABLE_EMAIL=true/false`, `ENABLE_WEBHOOKS=true/false`, `ENABLE_SAML=true/false`. When any is true, `scripts/start.sh` calls `shared-services.sh ensure` automatically. `ENABLE_EMAIL` also includes `compose/email-overlay.yml` so Metabase gets SMTP env vars pointing at the `mailpit` container. `ENABLE_WEBHOOKS` sets `MB_HTTP_CHANNEL_HOST_STRATEGY=allow-private` (required — default `external-only` blocks all Docker network IPs). `ENABLE_SAML` starts Keycloak.
- Keycloak shared service: image `quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.2`, runs in `start-dev` mode (admin / admin). `KC_HTTP_PORT` and the host port mapping both use `${KEYCLOAK_PORT:-8180}` (same value on both sides of the `:` in the `ports:` mapping), and `KC_HOSTNAME_URL` is set to `http://keycloak:${KEYCLOAK_PORT:-8180}` — **not** `localhost`. This makes the single hostname `keycloak` resolvable both from inside Docker (via Compose DNS on the `mb_shared` network, hitting the container's internal listener) and from the host machine's browser, **provided you add `127.0.0.1 keycloak` to the Windows hosts file** (`C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts`, requires an elevated editor). Without that hosts entry, only the Docker-side resolution works and browser-driven flows (SAML redirect, OIDC authorization) will fail to reach Keycloak.
  - Why this matters for OIDC specifically: unlike SAML (where the browser fetches metadata directly), Metabase's backend must call Keycloak's **token endpoint** itself, server-to-server, after the browser redirects back with an auth code. Since `KC_HOSTNAME_URL` controls every URL Keycloak advertises in its discovery document (issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, jwks_uri), those URLs must be reachable from *both* the Metabase container and the browser — hence the shared `keycloak` hostname + hosts-file entry, rather than the old `localhost`-only scheme (which only worked for SAML's browser-only metadata fetch).
  - For SAML setup: configure Metabase's IdP metadata URL as `http://keycloak:${KEYCLOAK_PORT:-8180}/realms/<realm>/protocol/saml/descriptor` (container-to-container fetch); the metadata XML will contain `keycloak:<KEYCLOAK_PORT>` endpoints, which the browser can also follow once the hosts entry is in place.
  - For OIDC setup: configure Metabase's OIDC **Issuer** field as `http://keycloak:${KEYCLOAK_PORT:-8180}/realms/<realm>` — Metabase fetches `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration` itself, and the resulting endpoints will all be `keycloak:<KEYCLOAK_PORT>`-based, reachable from both sides. The **Key** field in Metabase's OIDC form is a provider slug you choose (e.g. `keycloak`); it determines the callback URL: `http://<metabase-host>/auth/sso/<key>/callback`. Use this exact URL as the **Valid Redirect URI** in the Keycloak client settings — not the bare `/auth/sso` path.
  - `firefox-container.sh` now supports a `--remove` flag: removes the named container entry from Firefox's `containers.json`. Called by `nuke.sh` (when user confirms env deletion) and `remove-stack.sh` (for each dataset combo during stack removal).
- `MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` is set in `env/common.env` and wired into `compose/base.yml`. It is required for OIDC authentication — Metabase refuses to save OIDC settings without it. The value is shared across all stacks via `common.env`. Do not rotate it after OIDC secrets have been stored, as those values are encrypted with this key.
- `MB_HTTP_CHANNEL_HOST_STRATEGY` is a Metabase env var controlling outbound HTTP channel SSRF protection. `external-only` (default) blocks all private/RFC-1918 IPs and known metadata hostnames including `host.docker.internal`. `allow-private` permits Docker network IPs but still blocks loopback. `allow-all` removes all restrictions. Set via `compose/base.yml`; driven by `ENABLE_WEBHOOKS` in `scripts/common.sh`.
- The Metabase frontend has a Yup validation bug: the webhook URL field rejects bare hostnames (no TLD) such as `webhook-tester:8080`, even though the backend accepts them. Workaround: webhook channels are auto-created via `POST /api/channel` using `MB_AUTOMATION_API_KEY` in `scripts/start.sh`, bypassing the frontend entirely.
- Webhook session IDs are deterministic UUIDs derived from `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` (md5, UUID-formatted) — computed in `load_stack_env` as `WEBHOOK_SESSION_ID`. Same stack always gets the same session path, stable across restarts. The webhook-tester container runs with `AUTO_CREATE_SESSIONS=true` so it accepts any UUID path without pre-registration. Metabase POSTs to `http://webhook-tester:8080/<WEBHOOK_SESSION_ID>`; the user watches at `http://localhost:9000/<WEBHOOK_SESSION_ID>` (printed by `start.sh`).
- LLM debug logging: `METABOT_DEBUG_LLM=true` in a version env file (`env/mb_versions/*.env`) enables `MB_METABOT_DEBUG_LLM_REQUESTS=true` in the container, which writes one JSON file per LLM API call. Files land at `logs/ai/requests/` **relative to the JVM working directory** (`/`), so the container path is `/logs/ai/requests/` — not `/app/logs/ai/requests/`. The bind mount in `compose/base.yml` uses `source: ../metabot-debug-logs/${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}` (per-stack subfolder) so logs from concurrent stacks never intermingle. `start.sh` creates the host directory and runs `chmod o+w` on it (required on Linux because the Metabase JVM runs as uid 2000 while the host dir is owned by the script user; harmless no-op on Windows/Docker Desktop where NTFS does not enforce Unix UID permissions).
- **Metabase MCP server**: `make start` automatically registers the running stack as an MCP server in Claude Code (via `claude mcp add -s project`, written to `.mcp.json` which is gitignored). The MCP server name is `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` (e.g. `mb_1_62_3_x_sample_mysql8`), so multiple stacks each get their own named entry. `make nuke` removes the entry. MCP tools are only available in new Claude sessions started after `make start`. If the `claude` CLI is not on `PATH`, registration is silently skipped. To register manually: `claude mcp add --transport http <COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME> http://localhost:<PORT>/api/metabase-mcp --header "x-api-key: <MB_AUTOMATION_API_KEY>" -s project`. The `--header` flag is required — omitting it leaves the server in "Needs authentication" state and no tools load.
